cohort: 42 cases with a prenatal diagnosis of anencephaly who delivered after 24 weeks' gestation during the period 1990 until 2016
finding: Anencephaly was not associated with an increased risk of obstetric complications, however, there was a tendency towards delivery via repeated caesarean section in women with a previous uterine scar.
mod_finding: The rate of vaginal birth was 69% (29/42), the overall rate of caesarean section was 31% (13/42), with a primary caesarean section in 31% (4/13) and a repeat caesarean section in 69% (9/13) of the patients.
gest_age: Average of 36 weeks at birth (range 25-44 weeks)
